unreg:combine_testing_results.rederivation_notes: Own chain written before reading the record: (1) the field is the ~320-330 Combine invitees, not the draft class; (2) each invitee decides per drill whether to test (injury, agent strategy, pro-day deferral), a non-random thinning that often removes top priors; (3) each tester's recorded mark is the best of ~2 attempts around a ceiling predictable from track/sprint history, size and position; (4) the settled value is the max broad jump (vs a 148-inch rung, one inch above Byron Jones's 147-inch 2015 record) or the argmax of official 40 times; (5) settlement hazards from the text: Combine-only scope (pro-day marks excluded), no source of truth named, no unofficial/official rule, no tie clause for the fastest 40, rules_secondary empty. Inputs I listed: invite list, participation hazard + news, athletic prior, attempt noise, historical yearly-best/record tail, timing protocol, rules text, lifecycle (drill days vs close). After comparison the record matches my chain on every stage; differences are minor: the author restricts the broad-jump pool to WR/CB/RB/S (edge/LB/TE also produce 11-foot jumps), treats pool composition as a separate primary input although it is an aggregate of the per-prospect prior, labels a variance interaction 'convex' in a way that is wrong for the favourite, and asserts an unverified 2006 timing-era break. Settlement claims and both verbatim quotes check out against the sampled rules text.

findings.text: nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix (primary) is largely redundant with nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior + nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard: its own measurement counts 'invitees with a pre-Combine prior faster than 4.40 s', i.e. an aggregate of the prior. In a per-prospect simulation it adds nothing; it should be secondary/derived or used only for the historical GEV covariate.

Pool definition for the broad jump is limited to 'WR, CB, RB and safety' (s1, input why). Elite broad jumps also come from edge rushers, linebackers, tight ends and occasionally QBs; the broad-jump tail pool should be position-agnostic, filtered by prior rather than position.

Interaction combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k x prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior is labelled 'convex' ('probability of producing an extreme mark is convex in attempt variance'). This holds only for runners whose mean is behind the target; for the favourite higher variance lowers argmax probability. The sign depends on position relative to the leader; wording should say so.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'electronic era, about 2006 onward' / 'since electronic timing' is asserted without a source; Combine 40s are commonly described as electronically timed from about 1999, and any later timing-system changes (regime breaks) are not identified. Affects which history window is comparable for the extreme-value fit.

Series scope undisclosed: KXNFLCOMBINE is titled 'NFL Combine' and may list other drills (vertical, bench, 3-cone, shuttle, 40 thresholds). The catalog entry covers only broad jump and fastest 40; a bench-press or agility market would need a different pool (linemen) and priors. Should be listed as unresolved.

Stage s3 attempt-noise figures ('sd about 0.04-0.05 s per 40 attempt', '2-3 inches per jump') are presented as distribution facts without a source; they are plausible but should be flagged as estimates pending the proposed random-effects fit.

unreg:slate_extremes.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: season-threshold contracts (BLOWOUT >51.5 margin, HIGHSCORE >109.5 total incl. OT, GAMESPECIALS 225+ rushing yards) are first-passage events: P = 1 if already cleared, else 1 - prod over remaining games of per-game non-exceedance, with shared team-rating error adding dependence. Per-game tails need market-free team strength, QB state, mismatch, garbage-time policy, weather/roof, OT, and for rushing a carries x per-carry-tail compound. Weekly argmax contracts need integer team-score PMFs per team (key numbers), paired-score covariance, slate size/byes, the running within-week maximum once Thursday/early games finish, market close timing, and the 1/N rounded-down dead heat. Hazards from text: no stat source named; OT explicit only for HIGHSCORE (BLOWOUT uses score 'at the conclusion of the game'; weekly markets and GAMESPECIALS silent on OT); postponed/cancelled games unaddressed except 'originally scheduled'. Base rates I expected: post-merger max total 106 (CIN-CLE 2004), margin 59 twice (LA Rams 59-0 1976; NE 59-0 TEN 2009), 225+ rushing games occur roughly every one to two seasons. Differences after comparison: author misstates the rungs as all beyond records, omits within-week running state and lifecycle for weekly markets, omits the existing team-score PMF input it cites, and builds GAMESPECIALS inputs for rushing only.

findings.text: Factual base-rate error: variants_and_edge_cases says 'Rungs sit at or beyond historical records ... so most season contracts are long-tail NO events', and new input nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_rate is labelled 'record-level single-game rushing total'. Only the 109.5 total rung is beyond the post-merger record (106). A margin over 51.5 has happened post-merger (e.g. NE 59-0 TEN 2009, a snow game, and LA Rams 59-0 ATL 1976), and 225+ rushing-yard games are recurring (record 296; many 225+ games since 2000). Treating these as record-break tails would miscalibrate nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate and the tail fits; the base-rate input must be re-specified per rung.

Weekly argmax contracts (KXNFLWEEKGAMEHIGH, KXNFLWEEKHIGHSCORE) lack a within-week running state: after Thursday, international, early/late Sunday windows the realised scores condition the remaining argmax. nfl.slate_running_extreme_state is defined only for season maxima ('after each completed game: max |margin|, max total ... max rushing'), and m.lifecycle (when weekly markets close relative to the Monday game) is absent from the input list. Both change required data (in-week results by kickoff window, market close times).

Missing existing input: the weekly highest-scoring-team argmax and nfl.slate_max_tie_mass need integer team-score PMFs; the record's own measurement cites 'nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean style' but that catalog input (exists in NFL_input_index) is not listed. nfl.team_points_for_against_rates gives rates/means, not the key-number PMF that drives tie mass at the top.

Series coverage: KXNFLGAMESPECIALS is mapped wholesale but inputs cover only rushing (carry_count_forecast, rush_yardage_tail, run_defense, late_lead_clock_carry_yield). The rules_secondary explicitly references quarter-specific markets and the series likely includes passing/receiving/TD single-game rungs; those need passing volume, QB efficiency, targets and quarter-window distributions. u2 discloses the gap but the catalog input list and contract_types ('any player single-game stat over rung') claim generality the inputs do not support.

Overtime claims beyond the text: s6 and catalog mechanism cite 'overtime inclusion' generically, but OT is explicit only for KXNFLHIGHSCORE; for BLOWOUT it is inferred from 'at the conclusion of the game', and the weekly markets and the GAMESPECIALS full-game rung are silent. The settlement_definition should mark these as inferred.

Interaction own_team_rating_market_free x qb_scenario_rating_drop x deep_tail_margin_model labelled 'multiplicative': the backup-QB penalty is already a rating drop on the same scale as the talent gap, so the apparent product is the convexity of the GPD tail in expected margin (already listed as a nonlinearity), not a separate interaction. Risk of double counting.

Catalog mechanism says extremes come from games with 'dome or calm conditions'; that holds for totals but not margins (the 2009 NE 59-0 blowout was in snow; bad weather can widen mismatches). Weather sign should be split by contract.
Cancelled/no-contest games (e.g. the 2022 BUF-CIN game) are not addressed for season or weekly contracts; u1 mentions only postponement week assignment.

Blueprint 'season_stat' fits the season-threshold contracts but not the weekly argmax pair, which are slate-level game-score markets; and required_data lists the Kalshi contract-text dataset as feeding nfl.slate_max_tie_mass, which is a modelled quantity, not a rules field.
